catalog_locator: p. 185 (PDF page 21 of the archive.org issue scan sim_oceania_1952-03_22_3; saved file the copy we hold), §10 Atemble, first paragraph and the paragraph below …
catalog_quote: The language in the region of Atemble is of a different type phonetically from those to the north. There are many (ə) sounds, even in accented syllables. The system is exhibited in the table. [...] Syllables may be closed, e.g. o'mängen, arm. The vowel (ə) is the outstanding feature of the language, e.g. prədən, throat; ŋgəm, breast; pərpər, butterfly; gərvər, star. The stress tends to fall near the beginning of the word : 'abɛ, stone; 'u:run, road; it does not appear to change with the addition of a suffix, as e.g. 'u:runan, 'u:rnan, on the road.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: LOCATOR AND QUOTE. Opened (85 pp., archive.org sim_oceania_1952-03_22_3), extracted PDF p. 21 with extracted text and rendered it at 130 dpi. The page is printed p. 185, header 'LANGUAGES OF BOGIA', section '10. Atemble.' The quoted sentences are on the page image exactly as reported: 'There are many (ə) sounds, even in accented syllables.' (para. 1 of §10) and, in the paragraph below the phoneme table, 'The vowel (ə) is the outstanding feature of the language, e.g. prədən, throat; ŋgəm, breast; pərpər, butterfly; gərvər, star. The stress tends to fall near the beginning of the word : 'abɛ, stone; 'u:run, road; it does not appear to change with the addition of a suffix, as e.g. 'u:runan, 'u…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress tends to fall at or near the beginning of the word (the cited examples are word-initial: 'abɛ, 'u:run), and it stays on the same root syllable when suffixes are added. Given Capell's own second-syllable marks (o'mängen, sə'ragaran), the safer reading is 'left-edge (first or second syllable), fixed on the root', which is why the fixed: initial syllable reading is provisional.
new_statements.exceptions: Statement is hedged ('tends to fall near the beginning'). Capell's own marks include second-syllable stress: o'mängen 'arm' (p. 185, mark placement corrected in the corrigenda, Oceania 22(4): 317) and sə'ragaran (p. 187). Schwa is said to occur 'even in accented syllables'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms from a 1949 survey (informants at Bogia-area schools and the native hospital; some wire recordings). Capell notes stress is unchanged under suffixation ('u:run 'road' > 'u:runan, 'u:rnan 'on the road'). No phrase-level information.
new_statements.identity_note: Capell 1951-52 labels the variety 'Atemble' (after Atemble village on the Ramu). Z'graggen 1969:158-159 and 1971:61-62, 83 state that Capell's Atemble phoneme chart, grammar notes, text and wordlist 'belong definitely to the Anor language' [anj, anor1241] and not to the Atemple language [ate, atem1241] spoken at Atemple village. The catalog entry should therefore be filed under Anor with 'Atemble (Capell 1952)' as the source label. Villages of Anor per Z'graggen 1971:83: Iwam, Diugumbi, Asapi, Atsuvatapi, Ivagripi, Uliangupi, Ivarapi, Vavapi.
